question: Which of the following influential philosophers were born in Kerala in the eighth century?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shankara.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Adi Shankara (Shankaracharya) was born at Kaladi in Kerala in the 8th century CE (traditionally 788 CE).

• He was the chief propounder of the Advaita Vedanta (अद्वैत वेदांत) philosophy, which teaches non-dualism — the identity of the individual soul (Atman) with the Universal Soul (Brahman).

• He established four mathas (monastic centres) at Sringeri, Dwarka, Puri and Badrinath to consolidate Hinduism.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• His famous works include Brahmasutra Bhashya, commentaries on the Upanishads and the Bhagavad Gita, and hymns like Bhaja Govindam.

• He is believed to have attained samadhi at Kedarnath at a young age (around 32).

NOTE

• Chaitnya (Option 1): Chaitanya Mahaprabhu (1486–1534), a Bhakti saint from Bengal who popularised the Krishna-centric Gaudiya Vaishnavism and Sankirtana.

• Ramanuja (Option 2): An 11th–12th century philosopher from Tamil Nadu who propounded Vishishtadvaita (qualified non-dualism).

• Namdev (Option 4): A 13th–14th century Marathi Bhakti saint-poet from Maharashtra associated with the Varkari tradition.

question: Who was the constitutional advisor to the Constituent assembly of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is B.N. Rau.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sir Benegal Narsing Rau (B.N. Rau) served as the Constitutional Advisor (संवैधानिक सलाहकार) to the Constituent Assembly of India.

• He prepared the initial/original draft of the Constitution which was then examined and revised by the Drafting Committee.

• He was a civil servant and jurist who studied constitutions of various countries to frame the draft.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• B.N. Rau later became the first Indian judge of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) at The Hague.

• The Drafting Committee, headed by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, worked on his initial draft to prepare the final Constitution.

NOTE

• Dr. Rajendra Prasad (Option 2): He was the President (Chairman) of the Constituent Assembly and later the first President of India.

• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar (Option 3): He was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee and is regarded as the chief architect of the Indian Constitution.

• Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru (Option 4): He moved the Objectives Resolution and became independent India's first Prime Minister.

question: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution is borrowed from Australia?
option_3: Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme court
option_4: Removal of Supreme Court and High court judges
solution_text:
The correct answer is Concept of Concurrent list.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Concurrent List (समवर्ती सूची) in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Constitution of Australia.

• The Concurrent List (in the Seventh Schedule) contains subjects on which both the Union and the State governments can legislate.

• Other features borrowed from Australia include freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse, and the joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Concurrent List originally had 47 subjects; in case of a conflict, the Union law prevails over the State law.

• The idea of a three-list scheme (Union, State, Concurrent) was itself influenced by the Government of India Act, 1935.

NOTE

• Amendment of the Constitution (Option 2): The amendment procedure is borrowed from the Constitution of South Africa.

• Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme court (Option 3): This feature is borrowed from Canada.

• Removal of Supreme Court and High court judges (Option 4): The procedure for removal of judges is borrowed from the USA (impeachment-style process).

question: In May 2024, India signed a 10 year contract with _____ for the operation of Chabahar Port.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iran.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In May 2024, India signed a 10-year long-term contract with Iran (ईरान) for the operation of the Chabahar Port.

• The agreement was signed between India Ports Global Limited (IPGL) and the Port and Maritime Organisation (PMO) of Iran.

• Chabahar Port is located on the Gulf of Oman in Iran and is India's first overseas port project.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Chabahar Port gives India strategic access to Afghanistan and Central Asia, bypassing Pakistan.

• It is a key node of the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC).

NOTE

• Pakistan (Option 1): Home to the Chinese-operated Gwadar Port, which lies close to Chabahar but is not involved in this deal.

• Bangladesh (Option 3): A neighbouring country to India's east; not related to the Chabahar agreement.

• Yemen (Option 4): A West Asian country on the Arabian Peninsula; not a party to this contract.

question: Mission "SAGAR" is an initiative launched by which of the following country to extend necessary assistance, including medical and food supplies to countries in Indian Ocean Region?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mission SAGAR was launched by India (भारत) in May 2020 to provide COVID-19 related assistance, including medical teams and food supplies, to countries in the Indian Ocean Region.

• SAGAR stands for Security and Growth for All in the Region (क्षेत्र में सभी के लिए सुरक्षा और विकास).

• It reflects India's role as a 'first responder' and 'net security provider' in the region.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The SAGAR vision was first articulated by PM Narendra Modi in Mauritius in 2015.

• Under Mission SAGAR, INS Kesari delivered assistance to nations like Maldives, Mauritius, Seychelles, Madagascar and Comoros.

NOTE

• Bangladesh (Option 1): India's eastern neighbour; a recipient of Indian assistance, not the launching country.

• Australia (Option 2): A key Indo-Pacific partner and Quad member, but not the initiator of Mission SAGAR.

• Japan (Option 4): A Quad member cooperating with India in the Indo-Pacific, but not linked to this mission.

question: Who among the following was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kailash Satyarthi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kailash Satyarthi was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize (नोबेल शांति पुरस्कार) in 2014, jointly with Malala Yousafzai of Pakistan.

• The prize recognised their struggle against the suppression of children and young people and for the right of all children to education.

• He founded the Bachpan Bachao Andolan (Save the Childhood Movement) to fight child labour.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• At the time, he and Malala were the only Indian-Pakistani pair to share a Nobel Prize.

• Mother Teresa (1979) was another India-linked Nobel Peace laureate.

NOTE

• Amartya Sen (Option 2): He won the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences (1998), not the Peace Prize.

• Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar (Option 3): He won the Nobel Prize in Physics (1983) for his work on the structure and evolution of stars.

• Venkatraman Ramakrishnan (Option 4): He won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry (2009) for studies on the structure of the ribosome.

question: Which 7th-century mathematician and astronomer revolutionized the study of numbers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brahmagupta.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Brahmagupta (ब्रह्मगुप्त) was a 7th-century (598–668 CE) Indian mathematician and astronomer who revolutionized the study of numbers.

• He was the first to give rules for computing with zero (शून्य) as a number and to work systematically with negative numbers.

• His major work is the Brahmasphutasiddhanta (628 CE).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• He gave a formula for the area of a cyclic quadrilateral (Brahmagupta's formula).

• He worked at the astronomical observatory in Ujjain.

NOTE

• Patanjali (Option 1): The sage traditionally credited with compiling the Yoga Sutras.

• Salim Ali (Option 2): A famous 20th-century Indian ornithologist, known as the 'Birdman of India'.

• Srikrishna (Option 4): A revered deity in Hinduism, not a mathematician.

question: In July 2025, who has been appointed as Indian Ambassador to the United States?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vinay Mohan Kwatra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vinay Mohan Kwatra was appointed as India's Ambassador to the United States (संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका में भारत का राजदूत).

• He is a career diplomat of the Indian Foreign Service (IFS), 1988 batch.

• Before this posting, he served as the Foreign Secretary of India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• He has earlier served as India's Ambassador to Nepal and to France.

• He succeeded Taranjit Singh Sandhu as India's envoy to the USA.

NOTE

• Vijay Keshav (Option 1): Not associated with this diplomatic appointment.

• Vikrant Singh (Option 3): Not the appointee to this post.

• Amandeep Singh (Option 4): Not associated with this appointment.

question: In June 2025, Rajesh Kumar has been appointed as Chief Secretary of _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In June 2025, senior IAS officer Rajesh Kumar (Meena) was appointed as the Chief Secretary of Maharashtra (महाराष्ट्र के मुख्य सचिव).

• He succeeded Sujata Saunik, who retired from the post.

• The Chief Secretary is the top-most executive official and administrative head of a state government.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Maharashtra's capital is Mumbai; the Governor and Chief Minister head the state's constitutional and political executive respectively.

• The Chief Secretary acts as the chief coordinator and secretary to the state cabinet.

NOTE

• Bihar (Option 1): An eastern Indian state with its capital at Patna; not the state in this appointment.

• Haryana (Option 2): A northern state with its capital at Chandigarh; not linked to this appointment.

• Odisha (Option 3): An eastern coastal state with its capital at Bhubaneswar; not the correct state here.

question: In which month a national movement in India for inclusive AI leadership was officially launched in 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is April.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A national movement in India for inclusive AI leadership (समावेशी ए.आई. नेतृत्व) was officially launched in April 2025.

• The initiative aims to make Artificial Intelligence development inclusive, accessible and beneficial for all sections of society.

• It aligns with India's broader IndiaAI Mission to build responsible and democratised AI.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The IndiaAI Mission was approved by the Union Cabinet in 2024 to strengthen the AI ecosystem.

• India is also set to host the AI Impact Summit, underlining its push for AI leadership.

NOTE

• January (Option 1): Not the launch month of this national AI movement.

• March (Option 2): Not the correct month for the official launch.

• August (Option 4): Not the month in which the movement was launched.

question: The Indian Evidence Act, 1872 has been replaced by which law?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indian Evidence Act, 1872 has been replaced by the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023 (भारतीय साक्ष्य अधिनियम, 2023).

• It is one of the three new criminal laws that came into effect on 1 July 2024.

• It deals with the rules relating to admissibility and relevancy of evidence in courts.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The three new laws replaced the IPC, CrPC and the Indian Evidence Act respectively.

• The BSA incorporates provisions for electronic and digital records as admissible evidence.

NOTE

• Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 (Option 1): It replaced the Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860.

• Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 (Option 2): It replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973.

• Nyaya Danda Adhiniyam, 2023 (Option 4): This is not an actual law; it is a fictitious/distractor option.

question: Jal Utsav Campaign seen in news in 2024 is an initiative of _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is NITI Aayog.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Jal Utsav Campaign seen in news in 2024 is an initiative of NITI Aayog (नीति आयोग).

• The campaign focuses on promoting water tourism and water sports while raising awareness about water conservation and management.

• It aims to develop reservoirs and water bodies as recreational and tourism assets.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission in 2015.

• The Prime Minister is the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog.

NOTE

• Ministry of Electronics and IT (Option 2): Handles IT policy, Digital India and electronics; not the promoter of Jal Utsav.

• Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Option 3): Deals with trade and industrial policy; not linked to this campaign.

• NGO Pratham (Option 4): An education-focused NGO known for the ASER report; not associated with Jal Utsav.

question: Unified Pension Scheme (UPS), launched in _____ by the Ministry of Finance, offers an alternative to the New Pension System for central government employees.
solution_text:
The correct answer is August 2024.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) (एकीकृत पेंशन योजना) was approved/launched in August 2024 by the government.

• It offers an assured pension as an alternative to the National Pension System (NPS) for central government employees.

• It guarantees 50% of the average basic pay of the last 12 months as pension for employees with at least 25 years of service.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The UPS became operational from 1 April 2025.

• It also provides an assured family pension and a minimum pension of Rs. 10,000 per month.

NOTE

• October 2024 (Option 2): Not the month in which the UPS was announced.

• December 2024 (Option 3): Incorrect; the scheme was already announced earlier in the year.

• February 2024 (Option 4): Not the correct launch month of the UPS.

question: The headquarters of WADA are in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Montréal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The headquarters of the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) (विश्व डोपिंग रोधी एजेंसी) are located in Montreal, Canada.

• WADA was established in 1999 to promote, coordinate and monitor the fight against doping in sports.

• It publishes the World Anti-Doping Code and the annual Prohibited List.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• WADA's original office was in Lausanne, Switzerland, before shifting its headquarters to Montreal in 2002.

• Its funding comes equally from the sports movement (IOC) and world governments.

NOTE

• Paris (Option 1): Capital of France and headquarters of UNESCO, not WADA.

• Geneva (Option 2): Headquarters of the WHO, WTO and Red Cross (ICRC), not WADA.

• Vienna (Option 4): Headquarters of OPEC, IAEA and UNIDO, not WADA.

question: In ice hockey, the fences that surround the ice hockey rink are called as _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Boards.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In ice hockey, the low fences/walls that surround the ice hockey rink are called Boards (बोर्ड्स).

• The boards keep the puck and players within the playing area and are usually topped with protective glass.

• The area behind the boards and glass separates the audience from the rink.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Ice hockey is played between two teams of six players each on an ice rink.

• The objective is to hit the rubber puck into the opponent's goal using a hockey stick.

NOTE

• Zones (Option 2): The rink is divided into three zones (defensive, neutral and offensive/attacking) by blue lines, but these are areas, not the surrounding fence.

• Crease (Option 3): The marked area in front of the goal where the goaltender operates.

• Spikes (Option 4): These are studs on footwear used in field sports like athletics/football, not a feature of an ice hockey rink.

question: India's first e-waste recycling park is to be built in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India's first e-waste (electronic waste) recycling park (ई-कचरा रीसाइक्लिंग पार्क) is to be built in Delhi.

• The park is being developed by the Delhi government to scientifically process and recycle electronic waste.

• It aims to handle e-waste in an environment-friendly manner and formalise the recycling sector.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The e-waste park is planned to come up at Holambi Kalan in Delhi.

• India is among the largest generators of e-waste in the world.

NOTE

• Bhopal (Option 1): Capital of Madhya Pradesh; not the site of India's first e-waste recycling park.

• Kota (Option 2): A city in Rajasthan known as a coaching hub; not associated with this project.

• Dehradun (Option 3): Capital of Uttarakhand; not the location of the e-waste park.

question: In June 2025, 2 new Ramsar sites from which state has been included in the list of Ramsar sites in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In June 2025, two new Ramsar sites from Rajasthan (राजस्थान) were added to India's list of Ramsar wetland sites.

• The two wetlands are Khichan (in Phalodi) and Menar (in Udaipur).

• Ramsar sites are wetlands of international importance designated under the Ramsar Convention (1971).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Khichan is famous for hosting migratory Demoiselle Cranes (Kurjan).

• With these additions, India's total number of Ramsar sites crossed 90, the highest in Asia.

NOTE

• Odisha (Option 1): Home to Ramsar sites like Chilika Lake and Bhitarkanika, but not the state in this June 2025 addition.

• Gujarat (Option 3): Has Ramsar sites such as Nalsarovar and Thol, but was not the state added here.

• Maharashtra (Option 4): Has Ramsar sites like Lonar Lake and Nandur Madhmeshwar, but not linked to this update.

question: The Kailasa Temple built in the 8th century is in which of the following state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kailasa Temple (कैलाश मंदिर) built in the 8th century is located at the Ellora Caves in Maharashtra.

• It was commissioned by the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I.

• It is a monolithic structure carved out of a single rock, dedicated to Lord Shiva.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Ellora Caves are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and contain Hindu, Buddhist and Jain monuments.

• The Kailasa Temple (Cave 16) is considered one of the largest rock-cut monolithic temples in the world.

NOTE

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 1): Home to Khajuraho temples and the Sanchi Stupa, not the Kailasa Temple.

• Rajasthan (Option 2): Known for Dilwara Temples and forts, not this monument.

• Gujarat (Option 4): Known for the Somnath and Modhera Sun Temple, not the Ellora Kailasa Temple.

question: 'Rai' is a famous dance performed in which of the following Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Rai' (राई) is a famous folk dance performed in Madhya Pradesh, especially in the Bundelkhand region.

• It is traditionally performed by the Bedia community and is associated with celebrations and festivals.

• It is usually performed to the beat of the mridang/dholak.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Madhya Pradesh include Matki, Phulpati, Grida and Maanch.

• Madhya Pradesh is often called the 'Heart of India' due to its central location.

NOTE

• Punjab (Option 2): Famous for Bhangra (men) and Giddha (women) folk dances.

• Odisha (Option 3): Known for the classical dance Odissi and the folk dance Ghumura.

• Assam (Option 4): Known for the Bihu folk dance and the classical Sattriya dance.

question: 'Kakkarissi Natakam' is a satirical dance-drama of which of the following state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Kakkarissi Natakam' (काक्कारिश्शि नाटकम) is a satirical folk dance-drama of Kerala (केरल).

• It is based on the theme of Lord Shiva and Parvati appearing on earth in the disguise of a fortune-teller couple (Kakkalan and Kakkathi).

• It uses humour and satire to comment on contemporary social issues.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The dialogues are in a mix of Tamil and Malayalam.

• Kerala's other famous art forms include Kathakali, Mohiniyattam, Theyyam and Ottamthullal.

NOTE

• Gujarat (Option 1): Known for the Garba and Dandiya Raas folk dances.

• Maharashtra (Option 3): Known for the Lavani and Tamasha folk performances.

• Tripura (Option 4): Known for the Hojagiri folk dance of the Reang community.

question:
In the context of Budget, which of the following is included in the revenue expenditure?
I. Salaries of government employees
II. Pensions of government employees
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the context of the Budget, revenue expenditure (राजस्व व्यय) includes both salaries and pensions of government employees.

• Revenue expenditure is the expenditure that neither creates any asset nor reduces any liability of the government.

• Both salaries (I) and pensions (II) are recurring expenses that do not create assets, so both are revenue expenditure.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Examples of revenue expenditure: interest payments, subsidies, salaries, pensions and grants.

• Capital expenditure, in contrast, creates assets (e.g., building roads) or reduces liabilities (e.g., repayment of loans).

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, because pensions are also revenue expenditure, not just salaries.

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, because salaries are equally a part of revenue expenditure.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, as both salaries and pensions clearly fall under revenue expenditure.

question: Who was the last of the powerful Mughal ruler?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aurangzeb.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Aurangzeb (औरंगज़ेब) (reigned 1658–1707) was the last of the powerful/great Mughal rulers.

• Under him, the Mughal Empire reached its greatest territorial extent.

• After his death in 1707, the empire began to decline rapidly under weak successors ('later Mughals').

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Aurangzeb was also known as Alamgir ('conqueror of the world').

• He reimposed the Jizya tax and was known for his orthodox policies.

NOTE

• Babur (Option 1): The founder of the Mughal Empire in India, who won the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.

• Akbar (Option 2): The third Mughal emperor, known for his policy of religious tolerance (Din-i-Ilahi, Sulh-i-Kul).

• Shahjahan (Option 3): The fifth Mughal emperor, known for building the Taj Mahal; he preceded Aurangzeb.

question: What is the traditional belief about the effect of a government cutting taxes and running a budget deficit?
option_3: It promotes foreign investors to opt out from economy rapidly
solution_text:
The correct answer is It promotes consumers spend more.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The traditional (Keynesian) belief is that when a government cuts taxes and runs a budget deficit, it promotes consumers to spend more (उपभोक्ताओं को अधिक खर्च करने के लिए प्रोत्साहित करना).

• A tax cut increases people's disposable income, which raises their consumption/spending.

• Higher consumer spending boosts aggregate demand and stimulates economic activity.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• A budget deficit occurs when total government expenditure exceeds its total revenue.

• This expansionary fiscal policy is used to counter recession and boost growth.

NOTE

• It promotes consumers spend less (Option 2): Opposite of the expected effect; a tax cut raises, not lowers, spending.

• It promotes foreign investors to opt out from economy rapidly (Option 3): Not the traditional belief associated with tax cuts and deficits.

• It shows government irresponsive behaviour (Option 4): A judgemental view, not the standard economic belief about a tax cut with a deficit.

question: At what age did Mahavir Jain decide to leave his home in search of spiritual truth?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 30.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mahavira (महावीर), the 24th and last Tirthankara of Jainism, left his home at the age of 30 in search of spiritual truth.

• He was born as Vardhamana around 599 BCE at Kundagrama (near Vaishali) in Bihar.

• After leaving home, he practised severe penance for about 12 years before attaining Kevala Jnana (supreme knowledge).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• He attained enlightenment (Kevala Jnana) at the age of 42 at Jrimbhikagrama on the bank of the river Rijupalika.

• He preached the five vows — Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya, Brahmacharya and Aparigraha.

NOTE

• 25 (Option 1): Incorrect; Mahavira renounced worldly life at 30, not 25.

• 35 (Option 3): Incorrect age; he had already renounced home five years earlier.

• 40 (Option 4): Incorrect; this is closer to when he attained Kevala Jnana (42), not renunciation.

question: In which Indian text does the name 'Bharata' first appear?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rig Veda.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The name 'Bharata' (भारत) first appears in the Rig Veda (ऋग्वेद), in reference to the Bharata tribe/clan.

• The Rig Veda mentions the Bharatas as a prominent Vedic tribe, notably in the Battle of Ten Kings (Dasarajna).

• The name of the country 'Bharat' is traced to this ancient Bharata people.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Rig Veda is the oldest of the four Vedas and one of the oldest religious texts in the world.

• It is a collection of hymns (Suktas) organised into ten Mandalas.

NOTE

• Ramayan (Option 1): An epic (Itihasa) by Valmiki narrating the story of Lord Rama; not where 'Bharata' first appears.

• Meghdutam (Option 3): A Sanskrit lyric poem (Khandakavya) by Kalidasa, composed much later.

• Mahabharata (Option 4): An epic attributed to Vyasa; though it deals with the Bharata dynasty, the name appears earlier in the Rig Veda.
